tools.name: exec_command
tools.description: Runs a command in a PTY, returning output or a session ID for ongoing interaction.

workdir.description: Working directory for the command. Defaults to the turn cwd.

tty.description: True allocates a PTY for the command; false or omitted uses plain pipes.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding output. Defaults to 10000 ms; effective range is 250-30000 ms.

max_output_tokens.description: Output token budget. Defaults to 10000 tokens; larger requests may be capped by policy.

shell.description: Shell binary to launch. Defaults to the user's default shell. CONDITIONAL: omitted under local ZshFork mode; present in Direct mode.

login.description: True runs the shell with -l/-i semantics; false disables them. Defaults to true. CONDITIONAL: present only when login shells are allowed.

sandbox_permissions.description: Per-command sandbox override. Defaults to `use_default`; use `require_escalated` for unsandboxed execution.

justification.description: User-facing approval question for `require_escalated`; omit otherwise.

prefix_rule.description: Reusable approval prefix for `cmd`, only with `sandbox_permissions: "require_escalated"`; for example ["git", "pull"].

environment_id.description: Environment id from <environment_context>. Omit to use the primary environment. CONDITIONAL: only when multiple environments are attached.

additional_permissions.description: Sandboxed filesystem or network access for this command; only with `sandbox_permissions: "with_additional_permissions"`. CONDITIONAL: feature exec_permission_approvals (default false).

bounds.max_output_tokens: default 10000; may be capped by policy
bounds.timeout_ms: NO model-facing timeout_ms parameter in this version

behavior.shell: Runs the command through the selected shell with `-c` or `-l/-i` semantics; `tty=false` uses plain pipes despite the description saying PTY.
behavior.blocking: Waits up to yield_time_ms (default 10000 ms). If the command is still running it returns a numeric session_id; otherwise returns exit_code and output.
behavior.stdin: No stdin parameter. Use write_stdin with the returned session_id.
behavior.background: No separate run_in_background flag; a long-running command becomes a unified-exec session when it outlives the yield window.
behavior.truncation: Output is bounded by max_output_tokens and policy; response may carry original_token_count.
behavior.continuation: Poll/continue with write_stdin(session_id). No explicit EOF/close parameter.

chunk_id.description: Chunk identifier included when the response reports one.

wall_time_seconds.description: Elapsed wall time spent waiting for output in seconds.

exit_code.description: Process exit code when the command finished during this call.

session_id.description: Session identifier to pass to write_stdin when the process is still running.

original_token_count.description: Approximate token count before output truncation.

tools.description: Writes characters to an existing unified exec session and returns recent output.

session_id.description: Identifier of the running unified exec session.

chars.description: Bytes to write to stdin. Defaults to empty, which polls without writing.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding output. Non-empty writes default to 250 ms and cap at 30000 ms; empty polls wait 5000-300000 ms by default.

max_output_tokens.description: Output token budget. Defaults to 10000 tokens; larger requests may be capped by policy.

defaults.yield_time_ms: 250 for non-empty writes; 5000-300000 for empty polls

bounds.yield_time_ms: non-empty writes cap at 30000 ms; empty polls 5000-300000 ms

behavior.blocking: With non-empty chars, waits yield_time_ms (default 250 ms). Empty chars polls without writing and waits 5000-300000 ms.
behavior.stdin: Writes `chars` to the session stdin. There is no explicit EOF/close flag; empty chars only polls.

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description: The `apply_patch` tool can be used to edit files. This is a FREEFORM tool, so do not wrap the patch in JSON.

freeform_grammar.definition:
start: begin_patch hunk+ end_patch
begin_patch: "*** Begin Patch" LF
end_patch: "*** End Patch" LF?

hunk: add_hunk | delete_hunk | update_hunk
add_hunk: "*** Add File: " filename LF add_line+
delete_hunk: "*** Delete File: " filename LF
update_hunk: "*** Update File: " filename LF change_move? change?

filename: /(.+)/
add_line: "+" /(.*)/ LF -> line

change_move: "*** Move to: " filename LF
change: (change_context | change_line)+ eof_line?
change_context: ("@@" | "@@ " /(.+)/) LF
change_line: ("+" | "-" | " ") /(.*)/ LF
eof_line: "*** End of File" LF

%import common.LF

required: patch body matching the freeform grammar

behavior.input: Raw text, NOT JSON. First line `*** Begin Patch`, last line `*** End Patch`.
behavior.operations: Add File, Delete File, Update File (with optional Move to, context hunks, `*** End of File`).
behavior.atomicity: Patch verification failure rejects the whole patch; errors include `apply_patch verification failed:` / `Failed to parse apply_patch input`.
behavior.cwd: Patch filenames resolve relative to the environment/session cwd; no explicit cwd parameter.

tools.output_schema: text: `Success. Updated the following files:` or `No files were modified.`; failures are tool errors.
unknowns: Whether `include_environment_id` adds `*** Environment ID:` in this single-environment turn (conditional on multiple environments).

environment_id.description: Environment id from <environment_context>. Omit to use the primary environment. CONDITIONAL: multiple environments.

behavior.output: Returns a data URL (`image_url`) and, when applicable, the detail actually used.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description: Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly - large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

behavior.engine: ripgrep with fixed argv; supports regex, glob/type filters, context, multiline.
behavior.pagination: `offset` skips N entries then `head_limit` (default 250) applies; `head_limit=0` means unlimited, not zero results.
behavior.modes: content / files_with_matches / count; count is matching lines per file, not total matches.
behavior.output: Content mode returns matching lines (with -n by default); files mode returns paths; count returns per-file counts plus totals.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description: Execute a `${SHELL_NAME}` command. Use this for shell semantics - pipes, env, processes, git, package managers, build/test runners, anything genuinely interactive or multi-step.

cwd.description: The working directory in which to run the command. When omitted, the command runs in the session's working directory.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds for the command to execute. Foreground default 60s, max 300s. Background default 600s, max 86400s. Ignored for background commands when disable_timeout=true.

description.description: A short description for the background task. Required when run_in_background is true.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run the command as a background task.

disable_timeout.description: If true, do not apply a timeout to the command. Only applies when run_in_background is true.

behavior.shell: `<shell> -c 'cd <cwd> && <command>'`; each call is a fresh shell; no shell history/state.
behavior.stdin: stdin is closed immediately after spawn (`proc.stdin.end()`); no stdin parameter.
behavior.output: stdout and stderr are combined; nonzero exit appends `Command failed with exit code: N.`; timeout/interrupt produce their own messages.
behavior.foreground: Blocks until done. On timeout it is auto-backgrounded when TaskList/TaskOutput/TaskStop are active (default), otherwise killed.
behavior.background: run_in_background=true returns a task_id/pid/status immediately; completion arrives as an automatic notification.
behavior.spill: Foreground output over 50000 chars is persisted; the result carries task_id/output_size_bytes and an output_path; use TaskOutput or Read.

tools.name: Read
tools.description: Read a text file from the local filesystem. TEXT ONLY; images/videos use ReadMediaFile, PDFs/binary are refused.

path.description: Path to a text file or a kimi-file:// attachment reference in the current session. Relative filesystem paths resolve against the working directory; a path outside the working directory must be absolute. Directories are not supported; use `ls` via Bash for a known directory, or Glob for pattern search.

line_offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Omit to start at line 1. Negative values read from the end of the file (for example, -100 reads the last 100 lines).

column_offset.description: Zero-based character offset within the first line of a forward read, excluding its line-number prefix. Uses JavaScript string length in the displayed text. Copy continuation arguments from the previous result to resume a long line.

n_lines.description: The number of lines to read. Omit to read toward the end of the file. Results are bounded by max_chars, with continuation arguments when the requested range is incomplete.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters in the returned text, including line numbers and status. Omit for the configured default; requests above the configured maximum are capped.

behavior.text_format: `<lineNo>\t<content>` lines plus a status block; long lines are fragmented with `Next Read: {...}` continuation arguments.
behavior.encoding: UTF-8 direct; UTF-16 LE/BE auto-detected and transcoded (strict first, U+FFFD if malformed); other encodings, binary files, NUL bytes, PDFs, and non-text suffixes are refused.
behavior.negative_offset: Reads from EOF; if the tail range exceeds max_chars, newest complete lines are returned first and Next Read covers the earlier range.
behavior.column_offset: Forward reads only; offsets past the line or splitting a surrogate pair are errors.
behavior.media: Image/video files are rejected with a pointer to ReadMediaFile (when the model has image_in/video_in and the tool is active).
behavior.security: Sensitive files (.env, credential stores, SSH private keys) are refused; .env.example/.env.sample/.env.template and public keys are exempt.
behavior.spill: Read results are bounded by their own character budget and are NOT spilled again.

tools.output_schema: text content plus status; media handled by ReadMediaFile.
unknowns: Exact status-block wording for every branch; key continuation/encoding strings were captured.

tools.name: Write
tools.description: Create, append to, or replace a file entirely. Missing parent directories are created automatically. Write is NOT ALLOWED for incremental changes to existing files; use Edit instead.

path.description: Path to the file to create, append to, or completely overwrite. Relative paths resolve against the working directory; a path outside the working directory must be absolute. Missing parent directories are created automatically.

content.description: Raw full file content to write exactly as provided. This does not use the Read/Edit text view.

mode.description: Write mode. Defaults to overwrite. append adds content to the end exactly as provided and does not add a newline.

behavior.modes: overwrite replaces the whole file; append adds bytes at EOF without adding a newline.
behavior.parents: Missing parent directories are created automatically (mkdir -p semantics).
behavior.line_endings: Writes content literally: LF stays LF, CRLF stays CRLF.
behavior.read_before_write: Read before overwriting an existing file (policy). Write ignores the Read/Edit line-number view; never include line prefixes.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description: Perform exact replacements in existing files. Edit is mandatory for every incremental change; read the target before every Edit.

path.description: Path to the text file to edit. Relative paths resolve against the working directory; a path outside the working directory must be absolute.

old_string.description: Exact content to replace from the Read output view, without the line-number prefix. Use LF for pure CRLF files; use actual \r escapes where Read shows \r.

new_string.description: Replacement text in the same Read output view. LF is written back as CRLF only for pure CRLF files.

replace_all.description: Set true only when every occurrence of old_string should be replaced.

behavior.matching: Exact literal match against the Read view; line-number prefix excluded.
behavior.uniqueness: `old_string is not unique in <path> (found N occurrences). To replace every occurrence, set replace_all=true...` unless replace_all=true.
behavior.not_found: `old_string not found in <path>, the file contents may be out of date. Please use the Read Tool to reload the content.`
behavior.concurrency: Same-file edits are serialized by a write lock, but stale old_string still fails; do not issue consecutive Edits on one file without re-reading.
behavior.crlf: Pure CRLF files are shown as LF; Edit writes CRLF back. Mixed/lone CR shown as \r and must be matched with actual \r escapes.

tools.output_schema: text confirmation (updated successfully / all occurrences replaced).

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern. Results are files-only; directories are never listed.

head_limit.description: Maximum number of matching paths to return after offset. Defaults to 100. Pass 0 to remove the match-count limit. The character limit still applies: large pages are saved for Read, and a continuation offset is provided when more paths remain. Search time and output capture limits still apply.

offset.description: Number of matching paths to skip. Defaults to 0. Each call searches the current filesystem again; changes can shift results between pages.

path.description: Directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Defaults to the current working directory.

include_ignored.description: Also match files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

include_dirs.description: Deprecated and ignored. Results are always files-only - directories are never listed. Accepted only so older calls that still pass this flag are not rejected by parameter validation.

units.head_limit: paths after offset; 0 = no match-count limit

bounds.head_limit: default 100; 0 removes count limit but character/output caps still apply

behavior.pagination: offset/head_limit; when the page is truncated by character limits, output provides a continuation offset and may save the page for Read.
behavior.ignore: Excludes gitignored files by default; include_ignored=true includes them but still filters sensitive files and VCS metadata.
behavior.ordering: Results are returned in modification-time order (per native description/implementation; ordering is not a parameter).

tools.output_schema: text paths + optional continuation/limit notes; large pages may be saved for Read.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description: Search file contents using regular expressions (powered by ripgrep). Use Grep instead of shell grep/rg.

path.description: File or directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Omit to search the current working directory. Use Read instead when you already know a concrete file path and need its contents.

glob.description: Optional glob filter for which files to search, e.g. `*.ts`. Matched against each file's full absolute path, so a path-anchored pattern like `src/**/*.ts` silently matches nothing - use a basename pattern (`*.ts`), or anchor with `**/` (`**/src/**/*.ts`). To scope the search to a directory, use `path` instead.

type.description: Optional ripgrep file type filter, such as ts or py. Prefer this over `glob` when filtering by language or file kind: it is more efficient and less error-prone than an equivalent glob pattern.

output_mode.description: Shape of the result. `content` shows matching lines (honors `-A`, `-B`, `-C`, `-n`, and `head_limit`); `files_with_matches` shows only the paths of files that contain a match, most-recently-modified first (honors `head_limit`); `count_matches` shows per-file match counts as `path:count` lines, preceded by an aggregate total line. Defaults to `files_with_matches`.

-i.description: Perform a case-insensitive search. Defaults to false.

-n.description: Prefix each matching line with its line number. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`. Defaults to true.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`.

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`.

-C.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`; takes precedence over `-A` and `-B`.

head_limit.description: Limit output to the first N lines/entries after offset. Defaults to 250. Pass 0 for unlimited.

offset.description: Number of leading lines/entries to skip before applying `head_limit`. Use it together with `head_limit` to page through large result sets. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline matching, where the pattern can span line boundaries and `.` also matches newlines. Defaults to false.

include_ignored.description: Also search files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

behavior.engine: ripgrep; hidden files/dotfiles are searched by default; gitignored files require include_ignored=true; sensitive files always skipped.
behavior.pagination: offset then head_limit (default 250); head_limit=0 means unlimited, not zero results.
behavior.output_modes: content / files_with_matches / count_matches; count_matches is total matches per file, not matching lines.
behavior.path_glob: `glob` matches the full absolute path, so basename patterns are recommended.

tools.output_schema: mode-dependent: content text, filenames list, or path:count lines; includes numFiles/numLines/numMatches/appliedLimit.

tools.name: TaskList
tools.description: List background tasks and their current status. Entry point for discovering task IDs before TaskOutput/TaskStop.

active_only.description: Whether to list only non-terminal background tasks.

limit.description: Maximum number of tasks to return.

behavior.scope: Background tasks (process and agent kinds), including lost tasks when active_only=false.

tools.output_schema: text `active_background_tasks: N` or `background_tasks: N` plus task records (task_id, status, description, command/PID/exit code, stop reason).

tools.name: TaskOutput
tools.description: Retrieve a snapshot of a running or completed background task. Always non-blocking.

task_id.description: The background task ID to inspect.

behavior.blocking: NEVER blocks; returns the current status/output snapshot immediately.
behavior.preview: Fixed-size preview of the last 32768 bytes; full never-truncated log at `output_path`.
behavior.metadata: task type/status/description, PID/command/exit code for shell tasks, stop_reason/terminal_reason for early endings.

tools.output_schema: text: task metadata lines, optional truncation note `[Truncated. Full output: <path>]`, then `[output]` preview.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description: Stop a running background task. Only use when a task must genuinely be cancelled.

task_id.description: The background task ID to stop.

reason.description: Short reason recorded when the task is stopped.

behavior.effect: Stops any task type (process or agent), suppresses the terminal notification, and returns status/reason.
behavior.terminal: If already terminal, returns its current status and stop reason without error.

tools.output_schema: text: Wall time, task_id, status, reason.

tools.name: ReadMediaFile
tools.description: Read media content from a file as image/video content parts. Conditional tool: only registered when the runtime has fs (or an attachment store) AND the model declares image_in or video_in.

path.description: Path to an image or video file, or a kimi-file:// attachment reference in the current session. Relative filesystem paths resolve against the working directory; a path outside the working directory must be absolute. Directories and text files are not supported.

x.description: Left edge of the crop, in original-image pixels.

y.description: Top edge of the crop, in original-image pixels.

full_resolution.description: Images only: skip the default downscaling and view at native resolution. Fails with an explicit error when the payload would exceed the per-image byte limit; use region for files that large.

behavior.formats: Images and videos detected by suffix/magic; unsupported formats rejected.
behavior.downscale: Images are compressed/downscaled to provider byte/edge limits by default; `full_resolution` preserves native resolution or fails over budget; `region` crops at full fidelity.
behavior.output: text wrapper plus image_url/video content part; note carries mime type, dimensions, delivery kind.
behavior.gating: Registered by registerMediaTools only when image_in/video_in capability is present.

tools.output_schema: content blocks: `<image path=...>` / `<video path=...>` text plus media part; note with mime/dimensions/delivery.
unknowns: Whether ReadMediaFile is active for the current model route (depends on image_in/video_in).

notes: Kimi Read is text-only; images/videos are a separate conditional ReadMediaFile; PDFs and Office/binary formats are explicitly refused.
No native LS: Read's own prompt says use `ls` via Bash for a known directory, Glob for pattern search.
No MultiEdit and no apply_patch; incremental edits must use Edit.
Bash.timeout is in SECONDS, unlike Claude/DSH milliseconds.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" -> "List files in current directory"; "git status" -> "Show working tree status"; "npm install" -> "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: Sandbox escalation target; only advertised when the shell executor confines. CONDITIONAL.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user's current request. CONDITIONAL.

bounds.timeoutMs: default 120000 ms; capped at maxTimeoutMs 600000 ms; must be positive and finite

behavior.shell: `bash -c <command>` in a fresh shell per call; no persistent shell state.
behavior.workdir: Relative workdir resolves against the session workspace; otherwise executor default.
behavior.stdin: No stdin parameter and no PTY; command stdin is not interactive.
behavior.timeout: On expiry, promoteOnTimeout=true moves the foreground command to a background job (result kind `promoted`, jobId, timeoutMs, output) instead of killing it.
behavior.output: stdout and stderr kept separate; long output truncated to tail with `truncated` and optional `spillPath`.
behavior.status: Result is a tagged union: background | promoted | foreground.

unknowns: Whether sandbox_permissions is advertised in the current danger-full-access composition; the runtime context says no sandbox restriction, so escalation fields may be absent.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

behavior.text_only: UTF-8 text; non-regular files are rejected (`not a regular file`).
behavior.format: `<path>...</path><type>file</type><content>` with `${lineNo}: ${text}` lines and a footer: `(Showing lines A-B of N. Use offset=B+1 to continue.)`, `(Output capped. ...)`, or `(End of file - total N lines)`.
behavior.caps: Stops at limit lines, 2000 chars/line, or 51200 bytes; byte truncation sets truncatedByBytes and a continuation footer.
behavior.offset: Must be a positive integer; offset beyond EOF is an error (`offset X is out of range ...`), except offset=1 on an empty file.

unknowns: Exact model-visible footer punctuation is captured from installed source; minor rendering wrappers may differ.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

behavior.create_vs_update: Creates a missing file or fully replaces an existing one; no append mode.
behavior.parents: Missing parent directories are created recursively (writeFileAtomic mkdir).
behavior.atomicity: Writes through a private staging directory + fsync + atomic replace; preserves existing POSIX mode.
behavior.read_before_write: fs-observation-policy requires reading an existing file first; unobserved overwrite fails with `cannot overwrite existing ... without reading it first`.
behavior.output: Envelope `Created file` or `Updated file`; output value carries path/operation/before/after.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

behavior.matching: Exact literal match; CRLF in old/new is normalized to LF for matching; file line endings restored on write.
behavior.uniqueness: 0 matches -> `old_string was not found in "<path>"`; >1 with replace_all=false -> `old_string matched N times ... provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true`.
behavior.read_before_edit: fs-observation-policy requires a prior read unless the file was just created/edited in this session.
behavior.validation: empty old_string and old_string==new_string are rejected.
behavior.output: `The file <path> has been updated successfully.` or `... All occurrences were successfully replaced.`

unknowns: Exact output object fields are less important than the text; schema shown from tool output definition.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Large images are downscaled automatically; do not install image libraries or create thumbnails to inspect an image.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

behavior.gating: Only registered while an attachments service is mounted; execution also requires the current model route to declare image input.
behavior.formats: PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF, including extensionless files sniffed by magic; unsupported extensions are errors.
behavior.limits: Byte cap = min(maxImageBytes, maxMessageImageBytes); rejects image dimensions over maxImageDimension, pixels over maxImagePixels, or bytes over the deployment limits.
behavior.downscale: Large images are downscaled; output note includes original dimensions and a coordinate multiplier.

unknowns: Exact deployment image limits are runtime config, not captured.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

behavior.engine: Packaged ripgrep (`@vscode/ripgrep`) via subprocess, fixed argv; includes hidden/ignored files.
behavior.over_cap: Config sampleOverCapGlobResults=false in the base profile -> keeps the FIRST 100 paths, spills the complete list, and reports the saved path.
behavior.pagination: NO offset/limit parameters; a larger result is truncated/reported with a saved list.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

behavior.engine: Packaged ripgrep, fixed `rg --json` argv; file/line/text parsed without colon ambiguity.
behavior.pagination: NO offset/head_limit parameters; over-cap returns first 250 matches plus a spill path.
behavior.output: matching lines grouped by file with line numbers; only one include glob, no negation.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

bounds.timeout_ms: default 30000; capped at maxWaitTimeoutMs 600000 when wait=true

behavior.consumptive: Returns only output since the previous model read (consuming cursor), not a line window of the full log.
behavior.wait: wait=false returns immediately; wait=true polls until terminal state or timeout, then leaves the job running.
behavior.output: `text` delta (stdout then `[stderr]` section) + public job object (id/kind/label/status/detail/startedAt/finishedAt).
behavior.loss: If the cursor fell behind the ring buffer, text ends with `[some output was dropped from memory; full output: <spill paths>]`.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

behavior.scope: Jobs owned by the calling agent; returns running and finished jobs.

tools.output_schema: array of public job objects: id, kind, label, status (+detail), startedAt, finishedAt?

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

behavior.effect: Requests cancellation through the job registry; returns outcome `cancellation-requested` or `already-finished` plus the public job.
